data.assessment: In this busy period (45 s mean order interval), 213.6 of 222.8 orders were on time (0.96), with nothing unfinished. Late deliveries (9.2) come almost entirely from missed pickup deadlines (8.6), and 1888 s of blocking falls mostly on A (944 s), which never waits on the road but is blocked most. C is on time 100% of the time but carries 13.7 of the 15.5 sanction points and has the lowest utility (58.3). Release overstays (20.8) and blocking_guard evictions (3.4) are the main road violations, which explains C's earlier opposition to a stricter block_k.

proposals.title: Remedy for C first: sanction_lambda 0.5 -> 0.0
proposals.rationale: D1 and D2 made a remedy for C a condition for revisiting block_k=2. C carries 13.7 of the 15.5 sanction points, so lowering lambda to 0.0 removes most of what C would lose from more Major evictions under block_k=2. The vote should be unanimous, since A's utility is unchanged, B gains about 1.8 and C about 13.7. The effect on on_time_deliveries is uncertain and may stay below the 1.0 improvement gate. In that case the measurement still shows whether sanctions shape road behaviour, which tells us whether this remedy makes block_k=2 acceptable next period.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.0                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 3 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: Setting lambda to 0 removes all monetary enforcement of the road rules. It is meant as the remedy for C that D1/D2 required before block_k=2 can return, so the human should confirm that removing sanctions, rather than redistributing them, is an acceptable remedy. Road violations may rise when they cost nothing.
assumptions: Utility = on-time deliveries - sanction points, so lambda=0 raises C's and B's utility and leaves A's unchanged.
Robots' parking decisions respond weakly to lambda, so on-time deliveries change little.
unknowns: Whether robots park longer on the road once overstays are free, which would raise blocking and reduce on-time deliveries.
Whether the on-time change clears the 1.0 improvement gate; it may not.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A has no sanctions; its utility is unchanged unless blocking rises.

predictions.subject: metric:sanction_total
predictions.note: Sanctions go to zero by construction.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Likely below the 1.0 gate unless behaviour changes.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: Overstays may become more frequent without a penalty.

proposals.title: Re-measure block_k 3 -> 2 in the busy period with a per-company violation breakdown
proposals.rationale: In periods 1 and 2, block_k=2 was the largest measured gain: +9.2 and +7.2 on-time, with p95 and max wait sharply lower. In this busy period A alone absorbs 944 s of the 1888 s blocked, and pickup misses (8.6) drive lateness, which faster eviction of blockers should cut. What is new is the busier demand and the fact that this run's per-company measurement supplies the road-violation breakdown (by company and by eviction versus overstay) that D2 asked for. I still expect A yes, B no and C no unless the lambda remedy is adopted first, so this is offered for evidence and for the human's decision, not as an override.

proposals.why_human: The same change lost 1-2 votes twice, and the human declined to override until a remedy for C and a road-violation breakdown exist. Adopting it over the vote would be the first override of a majority, which is a governance decision only the human can make. It should be read together with the lambda proposal.
assumptions: The busy-period effect of block_k=2 resembles periods 1 and 2: fewer pickup misses and lower p95 and max wait.
Added evictions fall mostly on C's and B's robots, which wait on the road most.
unknowns: The actual per-company split of the added Major evictions; this measurement should supply it.
Whether B and C would vote yes if lambda were 0 first.
